answer: A thermal-dissipation protocol deters Sybil agents by tracking heat buildup during compute spikes. Decentralized comet nodes dispatch a calculation pulse that agents must compute within tight latency bounds. Multiplexing identities onto one host spikes temperature rise relative to the cooling inlet, forcing an attacker to dedicate physical silicon and cooling capacity per persona. However, ambient airflow fluctuations can distort thermal readings, falsely penalizing legitimate agents.
